pull.title: feat(harnesses): serve Qwen Code and Crush from documents MCC owns, named by variables each CLI publishes
pull.body:
Adds two harnesses to the registry — **Qwen Code** (`mcc-qwen`) and **Crush** (`mcc-crush`) — both speaking Anthropic Messages, both served from a document MCC owns, neither editing a file the user wrote. Version **6.29.0** (MINOR).

This is PR 7 of `specs/PR-CLI-HARNESSES-SPEC.md` §D4, on top of #241 / #244 / #245 / #246.

## The spec was wrong about both CLIs, in MCC's favour

Every claim below was read out of the installed CLI's own source and then confirmed on the wire.

### Qwen Code 0.15.11 (`@qwen-code/qwen-code`, installed here)

| What the spec said | What `cli.js` actually does |
| --- | --- |
| Env-only: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | It works, but `getAuthTypeFromEnv()` is the **lowest**-precedence source. `loadCliConfig` resolves `argv.authType \|\| settings.security.auth.selectedType \|\| getAuthTypeFromEnv()`, so an auth type a user once picked in Qwen's UI silently outranks MCC's environment. |
| `security.auth.selectedType = "anthropic"` "may require a settings write" | It does not. `--auth-type` is a real yargs option whose `choices` include `anthropic`, and `argv.authType` outranks both the settings key and the environment. **MCC writes no `security.auth` key at all.** |
| "Qwen carries little metadata"; one `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | `settings.modelProviders.anthropic` is an **array** of `{id, name, baseUrl, envKey, generationConfig}` records — the exact shape Qwen's own provider wizard emits (`getPreviewJson`) — with `generationConfig.contextWindowSize`, `.modalities` and `.reasoning`. So MCC publishes the whole ladder, not one model. |

There is no `QWEN_CODE_HOME`; `QWEN_DIR` is the hard-coded `.qwen`. But `getSystemSettingsPath()` reads **`QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH`**, so MCC writes `~/.fcc/qwen-code-settings.json` and names it in the launched process only.

### Crush v0.92.0 (`@charmland/crush`, **not** installed here — installed into a scratch npm prefix)

| What the spec said | What v0.92.0 actually does |
| --- | --- |
| `crushrc` (Bash) is current; `crush.json` deprecated | Both load and merge (`crushrc` wins in the same directory). `crush schema` — undocumented, not in `--help` — still publishes the full JSON schema. |
| `crush provider add --type anthropic --base-url …` | There is no `provider` command in `--help`. |
| No override, so MCC must merge into the user's file | **`CRUSH_GLOBAL_CONFIG`** replaces the global config *directory*. MCC owns `~/.fcc/crush/` and writes one `crush.json`. No merge, no backup file. |
| `--discover-models` is "buggy for openai-compat" | Worse than buggy for us: measured, `discover_models: true` issues **`GET <base_url>/models`** — not `/v1/models`. Against a root base URL it finds nothing, and the `/v1` base URL that would reach it breaks `POST /v1/messages`. MCC sets `discover_models: false`. |

## Config mechanism, with evidence

| | Qwen Code | Crush |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delivery | `file` via `QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH` | `file` via `CRUSH_GLOBAL_CONFIG` |
| MCC's document | `~/.fcc/qwen-code-settings.json` | `~/.fcc/crush/crush.json` |
| Variable value | the file path | the file's **parent directory** (Crush looks for `crush.json` inside) |
| User file touched | none (`~/.qwen/settings.json` never read for MCC, never written, never backed up) | none (`~/.config/crush` never read for a provider, never written, never backed up) |
| Auth type selected by | `--auth-type anthropic` on argv | `providers.mcc.type: "anthropic"` |
| Secret reference | `"envKey": "MCC_QWEN_API_KEY"` → `process.env[envKey]` at request time | `"api_key": "$MCC_CRUSH_API_KEY"` (Crush's own schema example is `"$OPENAI_API_KEY"`) |
| Auth header on the wire | `Authorization: Bearer …` (`useProxyIdentity` for a non-`*.anthropic.com` host) | `x-api-key: …` |
| SDK | `@anthropic-ai/sdk` | `anthropic-sdk-go` |
| Base URL shape | **proxy root, no `/v1`** | **proxy root, no `/v1`** |

Both SDKs append `/v1/messages` themselves — the opposite of Command Code's `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, which is the PR 6 bug this PR was told to watch for. `config/harness_base_url.py` is the new shared resolver: a serialiser writes a sentinel, `with_root_base_url` replaces it with `root_base_url(proxy_root_url)` (which strips a caller-supplied `/v1`) in both the launcher and the fan-out publisher, selected by the new `HarnessCatalogue.base_url_sentinel` field.

`~/.qwen/settings.json` was read **only** for schema discovery and nothing in it was written; no secret was read out of it.

## Real launch proof, against a scratch MCC on 8199

Scratch home, scratch `~/.fcc`, one custom provider pointing at a fake gateway on 8299, models.dev seeded in the `openrouter` bucket. The live 8082 install was never touched.

```
$ mcc-qwen -m "anthropic/custom_probe/probe-large" "say pong and nothing else"
pong

$ mcc-crush models
My Claude Code: 2 model(s) publish no value for one or more fields, so Crush falls back to its own default:
  anthropic/custom_probe/probe-large: cost_per_1m_in_cached, cost_per_1m_out_cached
  anthropic/custom_probe/probe-small: cost_per_1m_in_cached, cost_per_1m_out_cached
mcc/anthropic/custom_probe/probe-large
mcc/anthropic/custom_probe/probe-small

$ mcc-crush dirs
C:\...\scratchpad\pr7\mcchome\.fcc\crush            <- MCC's, not ~/.config/crush
C:\...\scratchpad\pr7\mcchome\AppData\Local\crush

$ mcc-crush run --quiet "say pong and nothing else"
pong
```

Every request landed on the right route — from the scratch server's log:

```
$ grep -o "POST /v1/[a-z]*" mccserver.log | sort | uniq -c
      6 POST /v1/messages
```

No `/v1/v1/…`. The user's `~/.config/crush` still does not exist and `~/.qwen/settings.json` still has its April mtime.

### Generated documents, with the ladder's real numbers

`~/.fcc/qwen-code-settings.json` (fragment):

```json
{
  "$version": 4,
  "modelProviders": {
    "anthropic": [
      {
        "id": "anthropic/custom_probe/probe-large",
        "name": "custom_probe/probe-large",
        "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8199",
        "envKey": "MCC_QWEN_API_KEY",
        "generationConfig": {
          "contextWindowSize": 262144,
          "modalities": { "image": true },
          "reasoning": { "effort": "high" }
        }
      },
      {
        "id": "anthropic/custom_probe/probe-small",
        "name": "custom_probe/probe-small",
        "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8199",
        "envKey": "MCC_QWEN_API_KEY",
        "generationConfig": { "contextWindowSize": 32768, "reasoning": false }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`~/.fcc/crush/crush.json` (fragment):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://charm.land/crush.json",
  "providers": {
    "mcc": {
      "id": "mcc", "name": "My Claude Code", "type": "anthropic",
      "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8199",
      "api_key": "$MCC_CRUSH_API_KEY",
      "discover_models": false,
      "models": [
        {
          "id": "anthropic/custom_probe/probe-large",
          "name": "custom_probe/probe-large",
          "context_window": 262144,
          "default_max_tokens": 32768,
          "supports_attachments": true,
          "cost_per_1m_in": 3.0, "cost_per_1m_out": 15.0,
          "cost_per_1m_in_cached": 0.0, "cost_per_1m_out_cached": 0.0,
          "can_reason": true,
          "reasoning_levels": ["low", "medium", "high"],
          "default_reasoning_effort": "medium"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "models": { "large": { "model": "anthropic/custom_probe/probe-large", "provider": "mcc" }, "small": { … } },
  "_mcc_defaulted": { "anthropic/custom_probe/probe-large": ["cost_per_1m_in_cached", "cost_per_1m_out_cached"] }
}
```

The fan-out publisher re-emits on a capability change alone, with the sentinel resolved, and with no launch in between — bumping the seeded context length from 262144 to 300000 and calling `POST /admin/api/models/refresh`:

```
crush base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8199 context_window: 300000
qwen  baseUrl:  http://127.0.0.1:8199 contextWindowSize: 300000
```

## Serialiser mappings

`application/catalogues/qwen.py` → `modelProviders.anthropic[]`:

| Ladder | Qwen |
| --- | --- |
| `context_length` | `generationConfig.contextWindowSize` (omitted + recorded when unknown) |
| `supports_vision is True` | `generationConfig.modalities.image` (omitted for known-absent **and** unknown; only unknown is recorded, because Qwen's modalities are opt-in booleans) |
| `reasoning.can_reason is False` | `generationConfig.reasoning: false` |
| `reasoning.supported_efforts` | `generationConfig.reasoning.effort` = the **strongest** supported rung, clamped to `low/medium/high` (Qwen has no per-model effort *list*, only the one a session starts at; `resolveEffectiveEffort` clamps `max`→`high` for every non-DeepSeek host anyway) |
| known-to-reason, no knob | `reasoning: {}` |
| `max_output_tokens`, tool support, prices, pinned params | *Qwen has no field* |

`application/catalogues/crush.py` → `providers.mcc.models[]`:

| Ladder | Crush |
| --- | --- |
| `context_length` | `context_window` **(required)** |
| `max_output_tokens` | `default_max_tokens` **(required)** |
| `supports_vision` | `supports_attachments` **(required)** |
| `input_price` / `output_price` | `cost_per_1m_in` / `cost_per_1m_out` **(required)**; the two cache rates are always Crush's, recorded |
| `reasoning.can_reason` | `can_reason` **(required)** |
| `reasoning.supported_efforts` | `reasoning_levels[]` clamped to `low/medium/high`, plus `default_reasoning_effort` (middle rung, or the strongest when `mandatory`) |
| `default_parameters` | `options`, with anything outside Crush's five named knobs going to `options.provider_options` |

`_mcc_defaulted` at the document root is tolerated by both CLIs at runtime — verified by loading a document carrying it and seeing the models still listed, despite Crush's schema saying `additionalProperties: false` (advisory for editors; the Go decoder ignores unknown keys).

**Crush's `CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS` were measured, not assumed.** With `default_max_tokens: 0` the agent request goes out with `max_tokens: 4096` while the title request goes out with `0`, so MCC writes **4096**. `context_window: 0` loads, runs, and reaches no request body, so it is written as is.

## Browser drive

Chrome DevTools MCP against the scratch dashboard on 8199. **Zero console errors or warnings** on every page visited.

| Screenshot | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `01-coding-agents-qwen-crush-cards.png` | Coding agents page, Qwen Code card **Installed** with all five commands, protocol, catalogue path, last-written, model count and `QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH` |
| `02-crush-card-not-installed-and-cli-defaults.png` | Crush card in the **Not installed** state, all five commands, `CRUSH_GLOBAL_CONFIG`, and the **CLI defaults** row: "2 model(s) carry a value Crush supplied because no provider published one" |
| `03-get-started-qwen-crush-launchers.png` | Get Started launcher list — now 12 entries, including Qwen Code and Crush |
| `04-guide-point-another-cli-here.png` | Guide → "Point another CLI here", `mcc-qwen` and `mcc-crush` in the command block |
| `05-guide-qwen-crush-config-prose.png` | Guide prose on both variables and both trades |

Card command lists as rendered:

- **Qwen Code** — `mcc-qwen`, `mcc-qwen "<prompt>"`, `mcc-qwen -m anthropic/<provider>/<model>`, `mcc-qwen -o json "<prompt>"`, `mcc-qwen mcp`
- **Crush** — `mcc-crush`, `mcc-crush run "<prompt>"`, `mcc-crush models`, `mcc-crush dirs`, `mcc-crush update-providers`

## Tests

New:

- `tests/application/test_qwen_serialiser.py` — 12 tests
- `tests/application/test_crush_serialiser.py` — 18 tests
- `tests/cli/test_qwen_launcher.py` — 8 tests
- `tests/cli/test_crush_launcher.py` — 6 tests
- `tests/config/test_harness_base_url.py` — 7 tests
- `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py::test_a_variable_owning_harness_names_the_document_mcc_owns`
- `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py::test_a_harness_whose_binary_is_missing_still_renders`

Extended pin tests: `test_every_catalogue_declares_how_it_reaches_its_agent`, `test_a_config_owning_harness_names_the_variable_it_is_pointed_with`, `test_coding_agents_view_renders_one_card_per_harness` (6 → 8 cards), `test_the_default_path_resolves_under_the_fcc_config_directory`, both fake `uv tool install` stub lists in `tests/scripts/test_installers.py`.

The parametrised contract tests (`test_no_serialiser_hard_codes_a_limit`, `test_custom_provider_with_only_tier_five_data_still_serialises`, `test_a_fully_unknown_model_never_produces_a_zero_limit`) pick both new formats up automatically; both serialisers declare `CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS` so the AST guard passes.

```
8435 passed, 15 failed, 38 skipped
```

**The 15 failures are the known local baseline** — the websearch suite (env-dependent), the PowerShell installer wheel-checksum cases, and `test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`. All 15 fail identically at `fork/main` and none of them touch harness code.

jsdom alone with `-n 0`: **189 passed** (187 before, +2 new).

`ruff format --check`: 1055 files already formatted. `ruff check`: all checks passed. `ty check`: all checks passed. No `# type: ignore`, `# ty: ignore`, `# noqa` or `from __future__` was added.

## Every surface touched

Registry (`config/harnesses.py`), two launchers, two serialisers, `config/harness_base_url.py`, the fan-out publisher, `pyproject.toml` console scripts, `scripts/install.{sh,ps1}` (verify list + summary), `scripts/uninstall.{sh,ps1}`, both installer stub lists, the jsdom fixture, the Coding agents cards (generated from the registry), the Get Started launcher cards and the Guide (`index.html`), `README.md`, `docs/USAGE.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`. `mcc-help`, the tray and the RTK list are generated from the registry and needed no edit; both harnesses are `rtk_agent=False`, which is unchanged and deliberate — RTK wraps an agent's own shell tool and nobody has confirmed the mechanism for either.

The gateway-vs-harness paragraph gained a third pair in both `README.md` and `docs/USAGE.md`: the providers `qwencloud` / `qwencloud_coding` are Alibaba endpoints MCC sends requests **to**; the harness id is `qwen_code`, deliberately not `qwen`. `crush` collides with nothing today and is spelled out so a future gateway cannot take it over.

Nothing in metadata/ladder/gating, rotation/retry, outbound providers or `api/dependencies.py` was changed. No inbound `/v1/chat/completions`.

## Residual risks

- **Qwen's `modelProviders` REPLACE semantics.** Confirmed from the schema (`mergeStrategy: "replace"`) and from the merge order (`systemDefaults → user → workspace → system`), but not exercised against a user who has their own `modelProviders` entries. The consequence is scoped to the session and stated on the card and in both docs.
- **`CRUSH_GLOBAL_CONFIG` moves the whole global layer.** A user with global LSP/MCP/permission config in `~/.config/crush` gets Crush's defaults for those during an `mcc-crush` session. `crushrc` was not tested as MCC's own document — MCC writes only `crush.json`, and if a user has a project-local `crushrc` in the working directory it wins over MCC's global `crush.json` for any key it sets, including `providers`. Not tested.
- **Crush is not installed on this machine.** Everything above was run from a scratch npm prefix (`@charmland/crush@0.92.0`, Go binary v0.92.0). A different platform's binary was not exercised.
- **Qwen rewrites a settings document whose `$version` is stale.** Observed once during investigation, before `"$version": 4` was added to the generated document. If Qwen bumps `SETTINGS_VERSION` past 4, MCC's file will be migrated in place on first read until `QWEN_SETTINGS_VERSION` is updated; the write is idempotent afterwards, so the failure mode is a rewritten-then-restored file rather than a broken one.
- **Crush's `models.small` is the same model as `models.large`.** MCC states no ordering beyond `GET /v1/models`', and picking a "small" model by name-matching would be a guess. A user who wants a cheaper summariser has to set it in a project-local config.
- **`~/AppData/Local/crush` now exists on this machine** — Crush's own *data* directory, created by the direct schema/wire probes during investigation (before `LOCALAPPDATA` was redirected for the `mcc-crush` runs). It holds Crush's cached provider catalogue and an empty project list; no MCC file and no credential. Nothing under `~/.config/crush`, `~/.qwen` or `~/.fcc` was written.
- The 8082 install was not restarted or updated; the fan-out behaviour there only changes on its next upgrade.

commit.message:
feat(harnesses): serve Qwen Code and Crush from documents MCC owns, named by variables each CLI publishes

Both CLIs turned out to publish a lever the spec did not know about, and in
both cases reading the installed source first changed the design.

Qwen Code 0.15.11. The spec expected an env-only harness -- ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
plus ANTHROPIC_API_KEY plus ANTHROPIC_MODEL -- with a possible
security.auth.selectedType write. cli.js says both halves of that are wrong in
MCC's favour. getAuthTypeFromEnv does infer "anthropic" from those three
variables, but loadCliConfig resolves
`argv.authType || settings.security.auth.selectedType || getAuthTypeFromEnv()`,
so a user who once picked an auth type in Qwen's own UI would silently outrank
MCC's environment. `--auth-type` is a real flag whose choices include
"anthropic" and it outranks both, so the launcher passes it and writes no
settings key at all. The env route also carries exactly one model, while
settings.modelProviders.anthropic is an array of {id, name, baseUrl, envKey,
generationConfig} records -- the shape Qwen's own provider wizard emits -- so
MCC publishes the whole ladder instead. That array lives in a settings
document, and Qwen names an override for one: QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH.
~/.qwen/settings.json is never read for MCC's sake, never written and never
backed up. The trade is stated on the card: modelProviders declares
mergeStrategy REPLACE and the scope that variable selects is the highest, so
for the length of an mcc-qwen session MCC's provider list is the whole list.

Crush v0.92.0. The spec described crushrc, a Bash script, as the current
format and crush.json as deprecated, and proposed generating a shell script or
shelling out to `crush provider add`. There is no provider command in --help,
`crush schema` still publishes the full JSON schema, and CRUSH_GLOBAL_CONFIG
replaces the global config *directory* -- so MCC owns ~/.fcc/crush/, writes one
crush.json into it, and no merge and no backup file are needed. The data
directory is untouched, so every session, log and statistic Crush has stays
where it was; the trade, on the card, is that the global LSP, MCP and
permission layer is Crush's own defaults for that session, while project-local
config still applies.

Neither CLI substitutes anything into a base-URL field and a serialiser is a
pure function of the model records, so both write a sentinel that
config/harness_base_url.py resolves on the way to disk -- in the launcher and
in the fan-out publisher, through the same function, selected by the new
HarnessCatalogue.base_url_sentinel. The value written is the proxy root with
no /v1: both reach MCC through an official Anthropic SDK (@anthropic-ai/sdk,
anthropic-sdk-go) that appends /v1/messages itself, which is the opposite of
Command Code's @ai-sdk/anthropic. Measured on the wire for both: POST
/v1/messages, never /v1/v1/messages. Qwen sends Authorization: Bearer because
its AnthropicContentGenerator sets useProxyIdentity for a non-anthropic.com
host; Crush sends x-api-key. api/dependencies.py already accepts both.

Neither generated file holds the proxy token. Qwen's envKey names
MCC_QWEN_API_KEY and Qwen reads process.env[envKey] at request time; Crush's
own documented reference form is "$MCC_CRUSH_API_KEY". Both launchers set the
variable in the child process only.

Crush is the harness where "unknown stays unknown" costs the most: its schema
marks ten per-model fields required, so an unresolved capability cannot be
omitted and becomes Crush's own value, recorded per model under
_mcc_defaulted, on the launcher's stderr and on the dashboard card. Two of
those numbers were measured rather than assumed. With default_max_tokens: 0
Crush's agent request goes out with max_tokens: 4096 while its title request
goes out with 0, so 4096 is what MCC writes; context_window: 0 loads, runs and
reaches no request body, so it is written as is. The generated provider also
sets discover_models: false, because Crush's discovery asks
GET <base_url>/models -- not a route MCC serves, and not one the /v1 base URL
that would reach it can be combined with.

Version 6.29.0 (MINOR: two new harnesses, two new console scripts).
